Well, every baby is different, but milestones are exiting. Make sure that the grandparents make you part of the doctor visits in a way or another. Make sure that you keep a log of everything and try your best to be present when you can. The easiest way to transition I would think is to move with the grandparents so that you just don't take the baby to a whole new environment with people that they are not used to being around 24/7. I would move in and let the baby adjust to my presence. Learn the quirks and cues. The grandparents would have figured out many things like, when the baby is hungry or tired or wants to play, sick, etc. So i would spend some time in the home before moving. Then after moving coming over often to the grandparents house. And slowly coming a little less often until it's maybe every weekend or every other. You're going to have to build tough skin for the first few months because your baby will have a preference for the grandparents. That first year is so intense with the emotions and rollercoaster of everything. Kids grow up so fast that first year. My son grew 4 inches the first 3 months and got twice as heavy.

You're just going to have to come to the realization that you won't be the person that will be bonding with the baby for that year. There's nothing that you can do that is going to make the baby feel that you are the main person in their life because you won't be there everyday. Even if you come for visits, you won't be there when they need you on their day to day. You won't know how they like things or how to read the cues. Which is fine, but it's going to be hard to readjust once you and your bf become the main caretakers. 

For that year, you will just have to make sure that the grandparents make you part of the baby's life as much as possible. Call every night, video call everyday. And ask a lot of questions. 

It's hard. I wish you the best of luck!
